newsitem.title: USA: Conrail shrs run uphill after CSX offer.
newsitem.headline: Conrail shrs run uphill after CSX offer.

text.p: Conrail Inc shares soared almost 20 percent to 84-1/2 in Tuesday morning trade, closing in on the $92.50 per share CSX Inc offered Conrail in an $8.4 billion friendly merger announced before the market open.
In unusually heavy New York Stock Exchange trade, Conrail peaked at an all-time high 87-1/2, up from 71, then settled back to trade in the mid-80s.
By midmorning, Conrail's trading volume of over 2.4 million shares exceeded by 10 times its average daily volume.
Meanwhile, CSX shares suffered a three-point decline, or six percent, to 46-1/2, also in very heavy trade.
The agreement calls for Conrail holders to get a combination of cash and CSX shares worth $92.50 per share.
The combined rail company would have $14 billion of annual revenues and 29,645 miles of track covering a territory from Chicago, Boston and New York to Miami and New Orleans.
At least one competitor so far has said it will not be unheard from regarding the proposed combination.

In a statement, Norfolk Southern Corp said it "recognizes that the proposed merger of Conrail and CSX, if consummated, would have very significant implications for the nation's transportation system and for the shipping public. This combination raises serious concerns."
It said it will act "aggressively and responsibly" to protect interests of the shipping public, its shareholders and employees, and the communities that it serves.
On the NYSE, Norfolk shares rose to an all-time high 94-7/8 from 92, then eased to 94-3/4.
